review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–101) and grepped the repository for uses of its declarations. The file has three defs (unitBitStep, flatUnitWalk, unitJointDraw) and four lemmas or theorems about their laws. None carries a @[simp] attribute. Downstream users (UnitFiniteLaw.lean, AllSmallOuter.lean) and the file's own proofs apply these lemmas with explicit `rw`, `exact`, `.symm.trans` or `calc`. I found no use where a missing simp lemma, a wrong rewrite direction, competing rules, unwanted unfolding or a rewrite cycle causes a problem. Every law is stated with `mapLaw (uniformLaw ...) f` on the left and the target law on the right. Tagging them @[simp] would only add rules for niche expressions with no evidence of benefit. The two simp calls, `simp_rw [he]` and the `simp only [...]` in uniform_singleton_joint, use explicit lemma lists and look fine. I did not inspect the imported mapLaw and uniformLaw simp sets in detail. I cannot run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simplifier behaviour.
